clauses.reason: Terminated by its own terms: the order exempts the employee 'until March 31, 1935'. Recorded as 1935-03-31, inclusive (runs through the end of that day) under the owner's 2026-10-21 ruling; the exclusive alternative ends the exemption when that day began. Actor: EO 6088 itself. Later further-exemption orders recorded as later events: EO 6998 (March 30, 1935) recites that Bailey 'was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of 2 years by Executive Order No. 6088, dated March 29, 1933' and further exempts him until April 1, 1937; EO 7597 (March 31, 1937) recites EO 6088 and EO 6998 ('periods totaling four years') and further exempts Bailey until July 1, 1937.

research_rationale:
EO 6088 (March 29, 1933, Franklin D. Roosevelt). Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl has a heading naming EO 6088, its date (March 29, 1933) appears in the held text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. The dossier's original and clause text cite the APP page harvested live (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/DOCUMENTS.jsonl, sha256 f6ccd51d...), whose custody cannot be re-proven once the site changes; a common-crawl mirror capture of the same page is also held and registered (sha256 abbf450a..., MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl row with WARC location) and its text file is byte-identical to the live one (text_sha256 6103fadf... for both). The quoted clause words are therefore re-provable from the mirror capture, and the end cites the own-terms record taken from the registered mirror capture, whose custody copy is committed under jobs/cotton-capture-custody/output. Both page records were checked: each names EO 6088, its date March 29, 1933 appears in the text, and each text_sha256 equals the held file's. It exempts Harry O. Bailey, superintendent of meters in the District of Columbia under the Office of the Architect of the Capitol from section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 until March 31, 1935. Identity: number, date, person and end date agree across the APP page, the census register and the WPA 1944 numbered list. Legal reading: a single time-limited grant that ends by its own terms on 1935-03-31, inclusive. Later orders naming it, recorded as later events with their own dates and quotes: EO 6998 (March 30, 1935) recites that Bailey 'was exempted from compulsory retirement for a period of 2 years by Executive Order No. 6088, dated March 29, 1933' and further exempts him until April 1, 1937; EO 7597 (March 31, 1937) recites EO 6088 and EO 6998 ('periods totaling four years') and further exempts Bailey until July 1, 1937. Each recites this order as past history and grants a new period; none revokes or amends this order, so none is this order's end. Searches made on 2026-10-28: (1) census titles in jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv with retirement wording for the surname; (2) every WPA 1944 numbered-list entry (jobs/x1-class-engine/data/WPA_NUMBERED_ENTRIES.csv, whitespace-insensitive) for the surname with retirement wording; (3) a full-text search of every held order text under jobs/*/output/texts and jobs/*/data for the person's full name within reach of 'retire' or 'exempt'; (4) a citation search of every held order text for 'Order No. 6088' and list forms ('Orders Nos. ... 6088'). They found this order and the later orders recorded as later events, and nothing else naming this employee. Authority: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), whose proviso lets the President exempt a person from automatic separation at retirement age. No held source shows section 204 repealed or amended before this order's stated end. Held texts of later exemptions show the President still granting exemptions under section 204 through and after this date (EO 7725 of October 12, 1937, running to November 1, 1938, and EO 7842 of March 15, 1938, running to June 1, 1939), which corroborates that the statutory scheme ran through the stated date.
